SI-4_title.answer: Using normative modelling to detect disease progression in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease in a cross-sectional multi-cohort study

NM2-1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used adversarial autoencoders (AAE) for normative modeling. The AAE architecture included an encoder with two hidden layers (100 neurons each), a latent code of 20 neurons, and a decoder and discriminator with similar structures. The model was conditioned on demographic variables (age and sex) using one-hot encoding. The AAE was trained on 11,034 healthy controls from UK Biobank using Adam optimizer for 200 epochs with cyclical learning rate.
NM2-1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: In this paper, we developed the normative model using the adversarial autoencoder (AAE; Fig. 1). As an autoencoder, this neural network has an encoder and a decoder. ... The AAE is a blend of this autoencoder framework with adversarial training, which is used in generative adversarial networks modelling.

NM2-2_response_variable.detail: The response variables were regional brain volumes derived from T1-weighted MRI images processed with FreeSurfer 6.0. The final data included: (1) cortical volume for 68 cortical subregions (34 per hemisphere) parcellated according to the Desikan-Killiany atlas, and (2) volume of 33 neuroanatomical structures from whole-brain segmentation (Aseg atlas), totalling 101 regions/structures. Brain region volumes were normalized by dividing by total intracranial volume.
NM2-2_response_variable.supporting_text: We used the FreeSurfer software (version 6.0) to estimate the brain regions' volumes from the T1 weighted images. ... During this processing, the cortical surface of each hemisphere was parcellated according to the Desikan-Killiany atlas and anatomical volumetric measures were obtained via a wholebrain segmentation procedure (Aseg atlas). The final data included the cortical volume for each of the 68 cortical subregions (34 per hemisphere) and the volume of 33 neuroanatomical structures, totalling 101 subregions/structures.

NM2-3_explanatory_variables.detail: The explanatory variables were age (linear) and sex. Age was transformed into a one-hot encoding vector with 27 positions (corresponding to the age range 47-73 years). Sex was represented as a one-hot encoded vector with two positions (male/female). These demographic variables were used to condition the AAE decoder for reconstruction.
NM2-3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: In our analyses, we used a conditioned AAE. This type of autoencoder allows us to influence the model's reconstruction using the demographic variables, i.e. age and sex. To input these variables into the model, we transformed age and sex into one-hot encoding vectors. After this transformation, each subject has an age vector with 27 positions, where each position corresponds to a year within the range of 47-73 years. ... The subject's sex was represented in a one-hot encoded vector with two positions, one for male and one for female. The AAE's decoder used these vectors together with the latent code to reconstruct the brain data.
